newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia's Hun Sen leaves China for home.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen leaves China for home.

text.p: Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen left Beijing for home on Thursday, returning apparently without the blessing he had sought from King Norodom Sihanouk for deposing his son.
Officials said Hun Sen's special plane took off from Beijing at about 9.00 a.m. (0100 GMT).
Hun Sen held a five-hour meeting on Tuesday with the king at his residence in Beijing, where he has been receiving medical treatment.

Both sides were tight-lipped about the talks and there was no sign that Hun Sen had won the king's blessing for his power-grab last month in which he deposed Sihanouk's son, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Sihanouk said in a statement that he had called on Hun Sen during their meeting to restore peace in his homeland.
He also said that the Cambodian strongman had not accepted his offer to abdicate but had said that the king would be welcome to return soon to his homeland.

"This delegation -- in particular his excellency Hun Sen -- assured N. Sihanouk of its fidelity and its support for the king, whose offer to abdicate it did not accept," Sihanouk said in a statement issued on Wednesday.
Political analysts said Monday's abdication offer could signal Sihanouk did not want any part of Cambodia's political turmoil, sparked by Hun Sen's overthrow of Ranariddh on July 6.
Analysts in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh said Hun Sen had long feared the widely revered king would give up the throne, enter politics and challenge him for power.

The king said Hun Sen's delegation, which included new First Prime Minister Ung Huot and acting head of state Chea Sim, had welcomed his decision to return to Cambodia soon to hold a Buddhist ceremony for peace and reconciliation.
"My departure for Cambodia will take place well before the end of August," Sihanouk said on Wednesday.
Hun Sen had previously ruled with Ranariddh in an uneasy coalition government that took power after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
Sihanouk has so far withheld his stamp of approval for Hun Sen's administration, deriding newly appointed co-premier Ung Huot as a "puppet" and likening the situation in Cambodia to a "comedy".
Sihanouk said in his statements that he had asked Hun Sen to end the violence in Cambodia and work towards national reconciliation.
"I asked all of them to try to make an effort to achieve peace, cool down the situation and end war, insecurity and violence," Sihanouk said.

The king said he had asked Hun Sen and Ung Huot "to somehow achieve non-violence, national reconciliation, peaceful co-existence, solidarity, mutual respect, respect for human rights and our national constitution".

Chinese Premier Li Peng met Hun Sen and Chea Sim in the Chinese seaside resort of Beidaihe on Wednesday and urged the Cambodian leaders to respect the king and work for a peaceful resolution to the country's problems.
